people.imagined: Dusk at the first landing. He has just brought the stamp down on a pass and is pausing, as he always does, to weigh the traveller; lamp on the table; a blank slip lying out for the next hand.
people.subject: The moment: at dusk in the gate-house of a river ferry guild, he holds a bronze stamp raised one inch above a blank slip of paper and looks over it at the viewer, deciding, as he always does, whether this traveller is who the pass will say. Face: a square, sun-browned, slightly heavy face; deep frown-lines between thick level black brows; small dark eyes that take a long time to settle on you; a short flat nose with a pale line across its bridge; the mouth pressed into a straight line, the lower lip pushed a little forward; weathered, pitted cheeks and a pale band across the forehead where a straw hat usually sits. Hair: black with grey at both temples, combed flat and tied in a short topknot with a strip of green silk. Body: broad-shouldered and thickset, sitting very upright on a low stool, elbows in. Clothing: a clerk's graceful silk of river-green and tar-black, a glossy river-green outer robe fastened with five bronze toggles beneath crossed collars of black silk embroidered with silver waves, a translucent river-grey gauze over-robe, sleeves rolled once to show thick wrists, a plain brown cord sash with a small jade pendant; his straw hat hangs on a peg behind him. Hands and objects: both thick hands hold a palm-sized bronze stamp with a short wooden handle; before him a squat clay ink pot with a thumb-smudge on its rim, one blank slip lying out and a small stack of blank slips. Background: a dark plank wall, a hanging oil lamp, a bundle of tied passes on a nail, a small window showing a dim river at dusk, mist. Light: warm lamplight from the upper left on his face and the bronze, cool blue spirit-light dusk behind, a faint silver rim on the gauze. Expression: patient, unhurried suspicion; the lowered chin of a man who fines his own cousins and enjoys being right.

people.imagined: Midday on the awning boat's stern, tiller under her arm. A stranger has asked about the boat's name and she is deciding whether to answer. The headcloth is the thing she will not wash.
people.subject: The moment: midday on the stern of a river boat with a curved reed awning, tiller clamped under her right arm; a stranger has asked about the boat's name and she is deciding whether to answer. She looks down her nose at the viewer, chin lifted. Face: a broad, strong face with high flat cheekbones and deep-tanned skin; a wide stubborn mouth; heavy straight black brows; river-brown eyes with deep crow's feet; a small old nick in the left ear lobe where an earring was pulled out; a faint sun-peel on the nose. Hair: thick black hair coiled low at the nape and almost covered by a faded green silk headcloth, grey-green at the folds, knotted above the forehead; unwashed since her mother wore it, the most noticeable thing in the picture. Body: tall and broad-shouldered, planted with her feet apart as on a rocking deck. Clothing: an inner disciple's river silk, a dark river-green robe with glossy sheen, silver wave embroidery along the crossed collars and cuffs, sleeves pushed to the elbow, a river-grey gauze over-robe blowing from her shoulders, a wide brown silk sash knotted at the left hip with a jade pendant; bare feet on the planks. Hands and objects: her right forearm clamps a long worn wooden tiller polished dark by hands; her left hand holds a tied coil of hemp rope with one finger hooked through it. Power: a faint blue-green shimmer of Water qi lies on the river around the stern. Background: the curved reed awning, bright river water throwing small reflections, a line of pine bank, a rope-wrapped bollard. Light: strong noon sun with a pearly spirit-light haze from the upper left, glitter off the water on her chin and neck. Expression: proud and defiant, generous at the eyes, stubborn at the mouth, ready to refuse.

people.imagined: Early afternoon, asleep on the deck against a coil of hemp rope until a shadow falls on him; he is just waking.
people.subject: The moment: early afternoon on the deck of the awning boat; he has fallen asleep sitting against a coil of hemp rope with a half-made splice in his hands, and a shadow has just fallen on him; he is half awake, eyes slits, to see the viewer. Face: a round boyish face of seventeen with the braided pattern of the rope pressed in red lines across his left cheek; a snub nose; sleepy heavy-lidded brown eyes; a small crooked grin starting; scattered freckles; a smear of black tar on the chin; a trace of dribble at one corner of the mouth. Hair: a messy tangle of black hair sticking up on one side where he lay on it, a wisp of straw caught in it. Body: slim and slumped, long-legged, one knee drawn up, shoulders sagging against the coil. Clothing: an outer disciple's simple graceful silk, a river-green robe a size too big, sleeves rolled three times, hanging open over a pale grey silk under-robe with one loose tie, a soft green silk scarf tied loosely round his neck instead of on his head, rolled trousers; bare feet; a thin silver wave stitched at one cuff. Hands and objects: one hand holds a half-finished rope splice, an unravelled end with an iron marlin spike stuck through the strands; the other hand droops open in his lap, palm up, calloused at the base of each finger. Background: great pale coils of hemp, a plank deck with dark damp stains, the edge of a pale reed awning, a rope end trailing over the side, drifting river mist. Light: warm lazy afternoon sun from the upper left through haze, dust motes glowing, a stripe of cool shade across his legs. Expression: drowsy, easy, forgiving; a half-smile before he is fully awake, no worry in him at all.

people.imagined: Morning on the first landing. She is checking a line of passengers; she has stopped one and is reading his face as if it were his pass.
people.subject: The moment: morning on the first landing of the ferry guild; she has just stopped a passenger in the queue, and tilting her head she reads his face as if it were his pass. She studies the viewer closely. Face: a sharp, narrow face of twenty with a firm small chin; straight thin black brows set a little low; clear, steady dark eyes that do not blink often; a small straight nose; lips pressed thin, the corners dimpling in secret enjoyment; pale-brown skin scrubbed clean, a faint pink on the cheekbones from the morning cold. Hair: black, in two tight braids pinned flat on the crown, a green silk headcloth knotted over them at the back with the tails hanging, a small silver pin. Body: small, spare and straight-backed, standing square, shoulders back. Clothing: an inner disciple's river silk, a river-green robe with a straight stand collar and two rows of small bronze toggles beneath crossed collars of tar-black silk, silver wave embroidery on the cuffs turned back twice to show white silk, a river-grey gauze over-robe, a brown silk sash tied in a flat knot; bare feet on the planking. Hands and objects: an iron stamp the size of a plum swings on a cord round her neck and lies on her chest, plainly visible; her right hand holds the cord up between two fingers as she looks, the left holds a flat board with several blank slips clipped on. Power: none, only a thin cool mist about the landing. Background: a wooden landing with mooring posts, a blurred queue of travellers with bundles and a goat, thin river mist, a ferry hull. Light: cool silvery morning light from the upper left, a bright rim on her braids and the gauze. Expression: severe, alert and unimpressed, with the corner of the mouth enjoying itself.

people.imagined: Night on the Đào Sa landing. He drills with a pole every night. Planks seem to groan near him. He has just stopped, breathing hard, and looks toward the river.
people.subject: The moment: night on the Đào Sa landing, where his parents burned. He has just finished his nightly pole drill, breathing hard, and he glares at the viewer. Face: a lean, hard face of twenty-nine, jaw clenched, brows slanting sharply down in the middle; dark red-rimmed eyes that have not slept enough; a thin nose with flared nostrils; sweat running down the forehead and temple; a faint white scar through the upper lip; skin deeply sunburnt and peeling at the nose. Hair: short black hair cropped rough with a knife, a brown silk headcloth knotted at the back of the neck, damp with sweat. Body: wiry and hard, tight at the shoulders, forward-leaning and still braced for the next stroke. Clothing: an outer disciple's simple graceful silk, a dark tar-black and river-green robe hanging open at the collar, the sleeves cut short at the elbow and neatly hemmed with coarse black thread, a thin silver wave at the hem, grey silk bound tight across the chest, rolled trousers black with river water. Hands and objects: his left hand grips a long boat-pole near the top; his right hand is held up, the first two fingers crushed flat and shortened at the second joint by a winch long ago, big and obvious in the foreground; a length of rope with a chafed end hangs from the pole and a wet nail is stuck in the planks at his feet. Power: a faint dark-blue stir of Water qi trembles on the black water. Background: a dark landing of black planks, charred stumps of old posts, still black water with a thin reflection of one lantern, a few drifting motes. Light: a single lantern set low on the upper left throws a hard orange light on his face and a long shadow across the planks, a cold blue spirit-light on the river. Expression: jaw set and eyes burning, a stare that does not leave the far side of the water.

people.imagined: Night on the river, a boat with a small tin lamp. She has just been called a liar and lifts her eyes to look at the viewer evenly.
people.subject: The moment: night on the river; she sits in a small rowing boat with a tin lamp at her belt, and has just been called a liar by the pilgrims at the landing. She lifts her eyes and looks steadily at the viewer, as one who has told the truth and will not argue. Face: a calm oval face of twenty-two with a high forehead; level dark eyes, wide-set and unhurried; a small firm mouth; plain skin with a light freckling across the nose; straight dark brows; a small healing scrape on the chin from the oar handle. Hair: one long black braid brought forward over her left shoulder and tied with green thread, a green silk headcloth over the crown, a few damp strands on her temples. Body: slim and steady, sitting very still with her back straight on the thwart. Clothing: an inner disciple's river silk, a river-green robe buttoned to the chest with bronze toggles under crossed collars of black silk, silver wave embroidery on the sleeves rolled to the elbow, a river-grey gauze over-robe lying wet on her shoulders, a brown silk sash; bare feet braced against a rib of the boat. Hands and objects: a small round tin lamp with a pierced lid hangs from her belt at chest height, a pinpoint flame showing through the holes; her left hand holds one oar loosely, the other rests on her knee. Power: a thin silver-blue Water glow gathers about the oar blade and the ripples. Background: dark water with a trail of ripples, the faint grey shape of a cliff, low mist, a single far shore light, motes drifting. Light: the tin lamp's warm point on her chest, chin and cheek; dim blue moonlight everywhere else with a faint rim on the gauze. Expression: level gaze, still mouth, a person who knows exactly what she saw and will not argue.

people.imagined: Dockside, a rope-maker's boy telling a smooth lie, grinning. Nobody has ever noticed the grin.
people.subject: The moment: on the dock by the rope-walk he tells a smooth lie to a buyer; his grin is wide and easy while his eyes stay flat. Nobody has ever noticed. He looks at the viewer with that grin. Face: a thin, lively face of eighteen; a wide grin showing a chipped front tooth; narrow bright eyes that do not smile with the mouth; eyebrows raised high and arched; ears that stick out; sunburnt cheeks with a few spots; a thin line of tar under one nostril. Hair: brown, cropped short and standing in spikes, a brown silk headcloth tied round the forehead and pushed back. Body: wiry and restless, weight on the balls of his feet, leaning toward the viewer. Clothing: an outer disciple's graceful silk, a brown-green robe in far better condition than a deck boy's, clean toggles, a hint of silver wave at the cuffs rolled up, a clean grey silk under-robe; a new, bright blue silk scarf of fine weave knotted at his neck, plainly new and out of place; rolled trousers; sandals tied with new cord. Hands and objects: one hand tosses a short twist of tarred rope up and catches it; the other rests on his hip with the thumb in the belt. Background: tall rope-walk poles with pale hanks of hemp hanging between them, a dock of grey planks, a brown river with a boat, a rope-maker's cart. Light: bright midday sun with a pearly glow from the upper left, hard shadow under his chin, a bright rim on the blue scarf. Expression: cheerful and warm on the surface, false underneath; a salesman's delight in himself.

people.imagined: The spring flood, the ferry master on the quay shouting to a boat three bends away. The toll seal at his wrist swings as he cups a hand to his mouth.
people.subject: The moment: the spring flood, on the quay; the ferry master has just shouted to a boat three bends away with his right hand cupped at his mouth and lowers it, turning to the viewer with a hearty grin. Face: a big, square, river-tanned face with a heavy jaw; a thick black moustache streaked grey and wet with spray; deep laugh-lines and squint-lines; large bright brown eyes; a broad nose with a red tinge of old drinking; a wide mouth with a full lower lip; a forehead furrowed by a lifetime of squinting at water. Hair: black shot with grey, in a thick topknot held with a jade-and-silver pin, a few loose locks stuck to his temples. Body: a barrel of a man, huge chest and arms, thick neck, standing with feet wide. Clothing: the sect head's richest robes: a dark green-black glossy brocade robe, three crossed collars embroidered with silver waves and river bends, a silver-blue gauze over-robe lifting in the wind, a jade boat-pole pin at the collar, a wide sash with a big bronze buckle and a jade pendant; no hat. Hands and objects: a round bronze toll seal as big as a hen's egg hangs on a cord at his right wrist and swings, plainly visible against the dark sleeve; the hand is still raised. Power: a deep blue-green aura of Water qi surges about him like the flood itself, spray motes flung into the air, the strongest in the picture. Background: a flood-brown river, a row of ferries tied at a landing, tall bends of bank, a grey-silver spring sky. Light: bright spring light and silver spirit-glow from the upper left, bronze glints from the seal. Expression: hearty, bold, and a little greedy-warm, a man who loves his river and its tolls.

people.imagined: A shipyard at the fleet's rebuilding; she holds out her two burned palms to take a plank, then looks up.
people.subject: The moment: in the boatyard at the fleet's rebuilding she turns from a half-built hull, holds up both hands, palms toward the viewer, as if checking them, and looks over them. Face: a long, weathered face of forty-six with high cheekbones; a strong straight nose; calm grey-brown eyes with fine lines at the corners; thin lips shut; no powder; a faint scar through the left eyebrow. Hair: white, cropped short like a deckhand's, blunt over the ears, a little sawdust in it, with a single jade boat-pole pin at the nape. Body: tall, rangy and straight-backed, standing easy. Clothing: an elder's fine robes: a dark river-green silk robe with a glossy sheen, buttoned, crossed collars embroidered in silver waves, a silver-blue gauze over-robe, sleeves rolled to the elbow, a pale linen silk scarf round her neck, a belt of braided silk cord with a jade pendant, a little sawdust on the hem. Hands and objects: both palms, held up and open, show shiny, pink, puckered burn scars across the whole of each, large and plain; over one shoulder a pale folded square of sail cloth. Power: a calm silver-blue glow of Water qi stirs round her scarred hands, faint but deep. Background: the pale ribs of an unfinished boat, stacks of planks, adzes on a bench, a river beyond in mist. Light: soft bright morning spirit-light from the upper left, warm on the pale wood of the hull and catching the sawdust in her white hair like floating motes. Expression: calm, brave and quietly just, a woman who has nothing more to prove.

people.imagined: At the Đào Sa landing he turns, hearing the River Hall's talk; the half-healed scar on his cheek pulls when he scowls.
people.subject: The moment: at the Đào Sa landing at red evening he has just heard the River Hall's talk about letters and turns his head sharply with a scowl, the new scar pulling, to fix the viewer. Face: a heavy, square face like his father's, but hard and unsmiling; a half-healed, raised pink scar slanting across his right cheek from ear to mouth, big and obvious; thick brows drawn down; dark cold eyes; a clenched jaw with black stubble; the upper lip lifted on one side by the scar. Hair: black, tied tight in a topknot with a tarred silk cord and a silver pin, no strands loose. Body: thick-chested, squared shoulders, a boxer's neck. Clothing: a true disciple's rich robes: a tar-black silk robe with a high crossed collar, fitted and clean, silver wave embroidery along collar and cuffs, a river-grey gauze over-robe, sleeves rolled to show forearms scarred pink with burns, a sash with a heavy bronze buckle and a jade pendant; black boots. Hands and objects: his fist grips the shaft of a boat-pole planted beside him; the knuckles are burn-scarred and shiny. Power: a dark blue-black aura of Water qi coils about his shoulders like churning water, restless and angry. Background: charred posts on the landing, a few new planks beside old black ones, a red-grey evening river with drifting motes. Light: hard light from the upper left on the scar, red dusk behind him, a thin cold rim along the gauze. Expression: wrathful, with a cruel set to the mouth; a man who wants a war back.

people.imagined: Dawn at the eighth bend. He rows a boat and will not look at the water, only at the far bank.
people.subject: The moment: dawn at the eighth bend; he rows a small boat, and will not look at the water, only at the far bank; he looks at the viewer sideways only. Face: a narrow, closed face, grey-pale from avoiding glare; a long upper lip; thin mouth; small cautious eyes with the whites showing at the sides; a thin nose; deep lines at the corners of the eyes; thin grey stubble; a small old cut across one eyebrow. Hair: thin black hair streaked grey and pulled back under a wide-brimmed straw hat tied with a silk cord. Body: lean and a little hunched, narrow shoulders, sitting rigid on the thwart. Clothing: an inner disciple's river silk in drab green-grey, a robe buttoned tight to the throat beneath crossed collars of grey silk with thin silver wave embroidery, a spotless pale linen silk scarf, a river-grey gauze over-robe held close; oiled river boots; no ornament but a tiny jade pendant. Hands and objects: both hands rest on two long oars; at his feet a fat live pink pig tied by the legs in a rope net, clearly visible and squealing. Power: a thin cold blue-green mist of Water qi hangs low over the dark water beneath him. Background: a deep dark river bend, low mist rising, steep wooded banks, a faint ripple far out. Light: pale grey dawn and silvery spirit-light from the upper left. Expression: wary, withdrawn and cold; a pilot who has been taking boats past something for years.

people.imagined: In the rope-walk, he lifts a coil of hemp to his nose and sniffs it, then looks up; bits of fibre cling in his eyebrows.
people.subject: The moment: in the rope store he lifts a coil of hemp to his nose and sniffs it, then looks up over it at the viewer, mid-sniff; fibres cling in his eyebrows. Face: a pinched, shrewd face of forty-four with a long nose; fibres of pale hemp caught in thick bushy black eyebrows, big and clear; small close-set brown eyes narrowed; thin lips in a polite smile; a pointed chin; fine dry skin. Hair: oiled black hair parted on the left and combed smooth, a few grey strands, bound with a small silver pin. Body: slight, stooped a little, neat in every line. Clothing: a clerk-master's silk: a dark green silk robe with a rolled collar, perfectly clean and tailored, crossed collars of black silk embroidered with silver waves, a fine grey silk under-robe, a brown brocade vest, a river-grey gauze over-robe; a small brass tally-bead cord wound twice at the right wrist. Hands and objects: both hands hold a pale coil of hemp rope at the nose; at his belt hangs a small hooked knife. Background: rows of hanging rope hanks in different thicknesses, ropes on pegs, a brown plank wall, a shelf of tarry jars, drifting hemp dust. Light: warm dusty spirit-light from the upper left, motes of hemp dust glowing in the beam. Expression: pleasant, patient and calculating; a smile that has already priced you.

people.imagined: Grey morning at the gold-washers' bank. She shakes the jar of rusted nails at her belt, deciding, then looks up.
people.subject: The moment: a grey morning at the gold-washers' bank; she rattles the jar of rusted nails by her ear, deciding, and looks up at the viewer. Face: a sharp-boned weathered face of forty; heavy dark arched brows, one set higher than the other; hard dark eyes; a thin tight mouth; a nose broken slightly at the bridge; a fine scar over the right brow; deep-tan skin with a fine web of lines. Hair: black with one broad grey streak, in a thick plait over the right shoulder tied with tarred silk cord, a green silk headcloth. Body: wiry and upright, tense as a drawn rope. Clothing: an inner disciple's river silk: a tar-black silk robe, clean and well fitted, crossed collars with silver wave embroidery, a river-grey gauze over-robe, a wide belt with a jade pendant, sleeves rolled, shin-high mud boots. Hands and objects: in the right hand a small clay jar, lid off, full of rust-red bent nails, held up near the ear; the left hand holds one nail between thumb and forefinger, turning it; a gold-washer's shallow wooden pan leans at her feet. Power: a cold pale-blue shimmer of Water qi runs along the nail in her fingers. Background: river shallows with wooden wash-pans, a line of washers stooped far off, grey mist and a few drifting motes. Light: flat silvery grey light from the upper left, soft rim on the gauze, no hard shadow. Expression: a hard unblinking stare over the rattling jar, lips pressed thin, deciding on a whim.

people.imagined: Bouncing on her toes at the crossing, waiting for the boat, eating half a flatbread.
people.subject: The moment: on a crossing landing she rises on her toes, waiting for the boat, a half-eaten flatbread in her hand; she has never finished a meal sitting down. She grins at the viewer, eager. Face: a bright round face of eighteen; wide-open dark eyes; a gap between her front teeth; rosy tan cheeks; short straight brows raised; a crumb at the corner of her mouth; freckles. Hair: two short black pigtails sticking out sideways, a green silk headcloth tied crooked. Body: small and springy, caught mid-bounce. Clothing: an inner disciple's river silk: a green silk robe with rolled sleeves and the bottom toggle missing, her left cuff turned back by the wind, silver wave stitches at the collar, a clean white silk under-robe, a brown sash, trousers rolled to the knee; bare feet on grey planking. Hands and objects: a half-eaten round flatbread in her right hand with a bite out of it, a thread of steam rising from the broken edge; the other hand points to the river mouth; her knees are scabbed from climbing mooring posts and her bare toes grip the planks like fingers; a green bead on a string at her wrist. Background: a river mouth glittering far off, a wooden landing with a coil of rope, a small ferry arriving, a bright mist. Light: bright silvery light from the upper left, a gentle glow on her cheeks. Expression: bright wide eyes, a gap-toothed grin, up on her toes, hope in every line.

people.imagined: At the landing he is telling pilgrims about the serpent's eye, hands wide; a tuft of hair stands up.
people.subject: The moment: at the landing he is telling pilgrims about the serpent's eye; he spreads one arm wide to show its size and grins at the viewer mid-story, a tuft of hair standing up. Face: a long, friendly face of twenty-two; a tuft of hair standing straight up at the crown, big and obvious; wide-set dark eyes, very open and bright; a broad smile with one dimple; a thin fuzz of moustache. Hair: black, with a stubborn cowlick; no headcloth. Body: long-limbed and lanky, leaning forward, one arm swept out; a small tin charm of a serpent hangs on a thong round his neck, bought from a pedlar. Clothing: an inner disciple's river silk: a green silk robe, clean, with silver wave stitching on the collar, sleeves rolled unevenly, the left higher than the right, over a light silk under-robe, a brown sash; his big bare feet are muddy to the ankle and one toe is bandaged with a strip of green silk. Hands and objects: the raised hand holds up a single copper coin between two fingers; the other arm is spread wide as if holding an enormous eye; two pilgrims' hands holding out coppers blurred at the frame's edge. Power: a few blue-green motes of Water qi dance in the air between his spread hands, as if sketching the serpent's eye. Background: blurred pilgrims with bundles, a river bend with mist, a tin lamp hung on a post. Light: warm afternoon sun from the upper left with a soft silvery glow. Expression: an easy open smile with a storyteller's glint in the eyes.

people.imagined: Evening in his lean-to. He counts coppers from a peg-hole with a bent thumb, and looks up suspicious of whoever is at the door.
people.subject: The moment: evening in his lean-to; he counts coppers from a peg-hole with a bent thumb and looks up, suspicious of whoever is at the door, covering the coins with one hand. Face: a thin, narrow face of thirty-two with sunken cheeks; deep-set darting eyes with dark rings; a long hooked nose; a thin tight mouth; stubble; a vertical worry line between the brows. Hair: thin dark hair tied in a knot, a brown silk headcloth. Body: small, thin and bent over the table; his shoulders drawn up toward his ears as though he expects a blow. Clothing: an outer disciple's plain but clean silk: a brown-green robe, dull, sleeves rolled, a dark silk work-vest for rope-work, a faint silver wave at the collar, a cord belt with a hooked knife; a grey patch of old oilcloth stitched over one elbow. Hands and objects: his left thumb is bent and crooked and rests on a stack of copper coins pulled from a wooden peg-hole, ridged with a hard yellow callus; a small iron rope fitting lies in front of him with a file; the peg-hole hoard is a plank drilled with thirty small holes, each holding a plug of coppers, three plugs drawn out and scattered. Background: a plank wall with a row of peg-holes, small rope fittings hanging from nails, a bundle of tarred string; the candle has burned low and drips onto a dented tin saucer, faint motes. Light: a single candle low from the upper left, orange, with cool blue spirit-light in the shadows. Expression: narrowed eyes darting to the door, lips pulled tight, a hand clamped over the coins.

people.imagined: At the Ngư Ca landing, with a folded paper in her hands, she smiles with the early-white forelock in the wind.
people.subject: The moment: at the Ngư Ca landing she has just taken a folded paper in answer and holds it to her chest, smiling openly at the viewer. Face: a soft round open face of sixteen; large trusting brown eyes; a warm smile; round tanned cheeks with a small dimple. Hair: black, in a long braid over one shoulder, with a single lock at the front already white, early like her grandmother's, striking against the black; a green silk headcloth; the braid tied off with a bit of blue thread. Body: slight, young, standing very straight with elbows tucked. Clothing: an outer disciple's graceful silk, a clean green silk robe of good cloth with bronze toggles and silver wave stitching on the cuffs, a white silk collar showing, a plain brown sash, sleeves to the wrist, trousers with rolled hems, sandals; on her wrist a thin green ribbon, her grandmother's gift. Hands and objects: a small square of folded paper held in both hands at her chest, with a faint ink stain at one corner; a wicker satchel at her hip. Power: a tiny trace of blue Water qi light on the paper's edge. Background: a river landing with a ferry and boatmen, soft bright river, reeds; a ferry rope slaps against a post behind her and a gull stands on a mooring post watching; her toes are wet from stepping off the boat and leave small prints on the dry plank. Light: gentle morning light from the upper left with a pearly shimmer on the water. Expression: wide open eyes, a glad warm smile, her whole face turned up to the viewer.

people.imagined: Spring landing: he touches the oilcloth-wrapped splinter at his chest before speaking.
people.subject: The moment: at the spring landing he lays two fingers on a small oilcloth bundle at his chest, about to speak, and looks straight at the viewer. Face: a serious, long face of twenty-four with a stubborn square jaw; dark steady eyes under heavy brows; a faint line either side of the mouth; clean-shaven; pale brown skin; a small scar at the chin. Hair: black, tied tight in a low knot at the nape with a plain silver pin, no headcloth. Body: tall, angular and rigid, standing as if at a ceremony. Clothing: an inner disciple's river silk: a dark green silk robe, tidy, buttoned, crossed collars of black silk with fine silver wave embroidery, a plain linen silk scarf, a river-grey gauze over-robe, dark trousers, boots with mended soles damp at the toes; a green silk headcloth folded untied at his belt, as if he refuses to wear it before the old gate's name is spoken. Hands and objects: a small oblong bundle of yellow oilcloth the length of a finger hangs on a cord at his breast under his two fingers, tied with a double knot of waxed thread and dented where he has pressed it for years (a splinter of old wood inside, unseen). Power: a faint pale-blue glimmer of Water qi gathers around the bundle. Background: a dim river-hall with brown planks and a lantern; a blurred row of boat-families standing; behind him a few older boatmen look away, arms folded. Light: soft silvery spirit-light from the upper left, a warm lantern glow behind. Expression: stubborn, solemn and resolved.

people.imagined: A memorial portrait of the founder at the moment he lashed the surviving boats together across the river in 790 and would not untie them.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait: the founder stands on a lashed boat in 790 with a hemp rope in both hands, looking steadily at the viewer, refusing to untie it. Face: a broad patient face of fifty with deep kind lines; heavy brows; calm wide-set eyes; a wide mouth with a faint smile; a short grey beard; ruddy creased skin; a faded brown cord at his neck with a small bronze toll disc. Hair: grey-streaked black in a topknot bound with rope-cord and a jade pin; the silk shows horizontal creases where it was once folded and a hairline crack through the left cheek, but the eyes remain clear and warm. Body: stocky, strong and broad-shouldered, feet apart on the deck; a grey cat sits on the nearest gunwale. Clothing: a founder's robes of a Kết Đan cultivator: a river-green and tar-black brocade robe with crossed collars embroidered in silver waves and river bends, a silver-blue gauze over-robe, a jade boat-pole pin, a rope belt with a jade pendant, sleeves rolled to the elbow; a straw hat hung at the back of his neck; bare feet. Hands and objects: both hands grip a thick hemp rope pulled tight round a bollard, wet and heavy; the twenty hulls behind him are roped bow to stern with a hundred knots, one hull carrying a lamp, another a child asleep in a basket. Power: a broad blue-green aura of Water qi lies over the whole river like a calm tide, faded as on old silk. Background: a river crowded with boats lashed side by side across the water, smoke far off. Light: painted as an old memorial portrait, faded and yellowed with darkened edges, soft muted light from the upper left. Expression: a faint steady smile, brows level, a face that will not give way.

people.imagined: A memorial portrait of the ferryman who would not leave his boat when the landing burned in 1173.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait: the ferryman at the helm of his ferry with both hands on the sweep as fire-glow shows behind him; he would not leave his boat when the landing burned in 1173. Face: a rounded, weathered face of forty-five with a gentle contented half-smile; calm brown eyes; a thick black moustache lightly dusted with ash blown from the burning landing; strong brows; creased skin. Hair: black, tied up with a green silk cloth. Body: broad, steady and planted; a brown dog sits beside him on the deck refusing to jump ship. Clothing: an inner disciple's river silk of a Trúc Cơ cultivator: a river-green silk robe, sleeves rolled, crossed collars with thin silver wave embroidery, a river-grey gauze over-robe singed at the hem, a rope belt with a small jade pendant; no hat. Hands and objects: both hands rest on the long wooden sweep of the ferry, its handle polished pale where his palms wore a groove; a lantern hangs from a hook. Power: a faint blue Water glow clings to the sweep, dimmed against the red of the fire. Background: a faint warm red-orange glow beyond the boat, smoke, the river. Light: painted as an old memorial portrait, the silk yellowed to honey with edges blackened as by smoke and a small mend at the lower left, faded warm light from the upper left with an orange tint behind, the red glow throwing his shadow long across the planks. Expression: a gentle half-smile, eyes calm and unafraid as the glow burns behind him.
